full_judgment:
This revisional application arises out of the judgment and order of the learned Sub-ordinate Judge affirming those of the learned" Munsif in a proceeding under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 2. The petitioners before this Court are the co-applicants Nos. 3, 4 and 5-7 who were originally opposite parties Nos. 9, 15, 10, 11 and 38 respectively. The pre-emptor Makhan Lal filed an application under section 96(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act claiming preemption in respect of the, land transferred on 4.1.64. The opposite parties 9, 15, 10, 11 and 38 who joined as co-applicants claimed pre-emption on the basis of inheritance and as contiguous land holders. 

 6. Mt Syed Badrul Alam, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties relying upon a decision in the case of Bijan Bala Chowdhurani and others Vs. Maniruddin Biswas & ors. 24 D.L.R. (Dacca) 170, submits that the application of the original petitioner (pre-emptor) failed because it was not a valid application under sub-section (1) of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The co-petitioners cannot claim an independent right of pre-emption on the strength of sub-section (4) of section 96 of the said Act. According to him, the co-applicants having joined the application under sub-section (1) of section 96 cannot independently maintain their claim of pre-emption when the original application was filed on the ground of limitation. 

 12. Commenting on the case of Bijan Bala Chaudhurani (Supra), Mr. Hossain submits that the validity of an application under sub-section (1) necessarily refers to the initial validity and not the resultant ultimate validity. According to him, the averments made in the application under sub-section (1) are the criteria on which depend the initial validity of such application. In sub-section (1) and the proviso the necessary ingredients in favour of the claim of the pre-emptor have been mentioned. In sub-section (2) who are to be impleaded have been stated. In sub-section (3) (a) the necessary deposit together with the compensation has been `provided. When the pre-emptor satisfies these requisites, the court notifies the transferee and others who have been made parties under sub-section (2). Mr. Hossain therefore submits that the above said requirements if satisfied, make an application under sub-section (1) initially valid and the court assumes jurisdiction to act upon the application. Any other construction of the expression "when an application has been made under sub-section (1)," according to the learned Advocate may lead to an absurd position requiring the court to prejudge the matter before the claim is heard on evidence.
